script:
This humanoid learned to walk in a world that doesn't exist.
Before testing the skill on the real Figure 02, Figure trained its walking controller in a physics simulator.
Think video game, except every stumble teaches the AI how to adjust its next step.
It tries movements, gets rewarded for walking more like a human, and learns through trial and error.
The crazy part is they ran thousands of virtual robots in parallel, simulating years of walking in just a few hours.
And they didn't all get perfect conditions.
The simulation varied the terrain and the robot's physical properties, and threw in trips, slips and shoves.
That way, the robot isn't just learning to walk down one clean virtual hallway.
But the real world is never a perfect copy of a simulator.
Motors and surfaces don't behave exactly like the model, so a skill that works in simulation can stumble on the actual floor.
Figure says it bridges that gap by mixing up the simulations and using fast torque feedback on the real robot.
This is how robots can get years of practice before taking those steps in the real world.
And I think simulation is about to become the training gym for every robot.
